blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, cost accounting stops being an academic exercise and becomes a real guide to pricing and product decisions. The question "what does this product actually cost us?" sounds simple, but answering it honestly takes work. Direct costs — materials and direct labour — are usually easy. Indirect costs — supervision, warehouse space, utilities — are where most companies become creative.

A good cost accountant allocates indirect costs to products using a defensible rule, not a round number pulled from a meeting. Sometimes the rule is volume; sometimes it is space; sometimes it is complexity. The rule changes the numbers — and sometimes changes which products look profitable and which do not.

Without real cost accounting, pricing decisions are quietly made in the dark. With it, leaders can see which products are quietly subsidising others — and decide, explicitly, whether that is what they want.

items.q: According to the text, which costs are usually easy to work out?
options: Direct costs such as materials and direct labour
Round numbers agreed in a meeting
items.why: "Direct costs — materials and direct labour — are usually easy."

items.q: What does a good cost accountant use to allocate indirect costs?
options: A round number pulled from a meeting
The same rule as last year, whatever it was
A defensible rule such as volume, space or complexity
The price of the most profitable product
items.why: "allocates indirect costs to products using a defensible rule… Sometimes the rule is volume; sometimes it is space; sometimes it is complexity."

items.q: According to the text, why does the allocation rule matter so much?
options: It decides how many products a company can sell
It can change which products look profitable and which do not
It sets the salary of the cost accountant
It removes the need for direct costs
items.why: "The rule changes the numbers — and sometimes changes which products look profitable and which do not."

items.q: The phrase "where most companies become creative" suggests that the author…
options: is quietly critical of how firms treat indirect costs
admires how firms handle indirect costs
items.why: Inferência: "become creative" é irônico — o autor sugere que as empresas maquiam ou improvisam os custos indiretos.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The allocation rule should be defensible
Pricing without cost accounting is a decision made in the dark
It is fine to allocate indirect costs with a round number from a meeting
One product can end up subsidising another
items.why: Inferência: todo o texto defende regras defensáveis contra "a round number pulled from a meeting".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver conversando com uma nova gerente de produto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before you set the new price, let me show you something in these numbers. On paper, your product looks like the star of the range — a healthy margin, everyone's happy. But look at how the indirect costs were split.

Right now, supervision, warehouse space and utilities are all allocated by unit volume. Your product ships in high volume, so on that rule it should carry a big share of the overhead. But it doesn't. Someone rounded it down years ago, and nobody ever revisited it. The extra cost had to land somewhere — and it landed on the low-volume line next to yours.

In other words, that "weak" product is quietly subsidising yours. Once I allocate the indirect costs properly, by the space and supervision each line actually uses, your margin drops and theirs recovers.

I'm not saying your product is bad. I'm saying we've been pricing it in the dark. Let's agree a defensible rule first, rerun the numbers, and then decide the price with our eyes open.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How were the indirect costs being allocated when Oliver looked at the numbers?
options: By the margin of each product
By the complexity of each product
By the warehouse space each line uses
items.why: "supervision, warehouse space and utilities are all allocated by unit volume."

items.q: According to Oliver, what happened to the overhead that the star product should have carried?
options: It landed on the low-volume line next to it
It was paid by the supervision budget
It was removed from the accounts
It was shared equally across all products
items.why: "The extra cost had to land somewhere — and it landed on the low-volume line next to yours."

items.q: What does Oliver mean when he says the "weak" product is "quietly subsidising" the star product?
options: The star product will soon be discontinued
The weak product pays the salaries of the team
The weak product is sold at a discount
The weak product carries costs that really belong to the star product
items.why: Inferência: subsidiar aqui = a linha fraca absorve custos que deveriam ser da linha estrela, inflando a margem desta.

items.q: Why is the current rule a problem, in Oliver's view?
options: It is too complicated for the team
It was rounded down long ago and never revisited
items.why: "Someone rounded it down years ago, and nobody ever revisited it."

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's attitude towards the product manager?
options: Certain the product should be dropped
Coaching — he corrects the numbers without blaming her
Dismissive of her work and her product
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not saying your product is bad… let's decide the price with our eyes open" — ele orienta, não acusa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "For a junior analyst, costing is an academic exercise; for a manager, it drives real prices." An academic exercise is…
options: a task done for practice or theory, with no practical stake
a meeting with the finance team
items.why: Academic exercise = exercício acadêmico: algo teórico, sem consequência prática direta.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Materials and the wages of the people on the line are ___ costs — easy to trace to the product."
items.why: Direct cost = custo direto, ligado diretamente ao produto (materiais e mão de obra direta).

items.q: "Supervision, rent and utilities are shared across every product line." Utilities are…
options: useful tools kept in the warehouse
services such as electricity, water and gas
the managers who supervise the line
items.why: Utilities = serviços públicos (luz, água, gás) — custos indiretos típicos.

items.q: "We need a fair way to allocate the overhead across the products." To allocate means to…
options: distribute or assign something to different parts
items.why: To allocate = alocar, distribuir/atribuir os custos entre os produtos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the rule can't be justified, it isn't a ___ rule."
items.why: Defensible rule = regra defensável: aquela que se consegue justificar diante de questionamento.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre custos e preços. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new allocation rule." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new costing method across all product lines next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The product manager pushed back on the new numbers at first." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed the new rule but never followed through on updating the prices." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving a few cents off packaging won't move the needle on this product's margin." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não muda a margem de forma sensível.
